purpose: Controlled discovery vocabulary for classifying every physical heritage feature without restricting the archive to famous landmarks.

category_codes.label: Memorials
category_codes.description: Places or objects created to commemorate people or events.

category_codes.label: Inscriptions and plaques
category_codes.description: Individually identifiable written or engraved features.

category_codes.label: Street furniture and micro-details
category_codes.description: Distinct public-realm objects and small urban features.

category_codes.label: Public art
category_codes.description: Artworks installed in publicly accessible settings that are not better classified as monuments or memorials.

category_codes.label: Archaeology and historic remains
category_codes.description: Visible or officially recorded archaeological fabric and remains.

category_codes.label: Historic infrastructure
category_codes.description: Engineering and civic infrastructure with documentary or heritage value.

category_codes.label: Historic landscapes and designed spaces
category_codes.description: Historic parks, gardens, estates and designed landscape features.

category_codes.label: Industrial and transport heritage
category_codes.description: Physical remains associated with transport, industry and engineering.

category_codes.label: Cemeteries and burial art
category_codes.description: Graves, cemetery structures and funerary art.

category_codes.label: Commercial and everyday history
category_codes.description: Historic commercial and everyday objects visible in the built environment.

category_codes.label: Other documented feature
category_codes.description: A temporary holding category when no established category fits; review before publication.

feature_types.definition: A geographic place or complex that may contain many independently catalogued objects.
A distinct building, structure, monument or other main physical object.
A separately identifiable component or small feature with its own documentation value.
A continuous area or repeated physical sequence documented at an appropriate parent level.

classification_rules: Choose one primary category per record. Use research_notes to describe secondary characteristics rather than assigning multiple primary categories.
Use MICRO_DETAIL for an independently identifiable feature attached to a parent object; set parent_id to the parent record.
Use SITE for a larger place and create child records only for independently identifiable objects or details.
Use SURFACE_OR_SEQUENCE for a street, pavement, wall or repeated fabric; do not create a separate record for every indistinguishable stone or unit.
Choose the most specific category supported by the evidence. Do not infer age or heritage status from appearance alone.
Use OTHER only temporarily and review it during taxonomy maintenance.
